page.h1: HTS Chapter 52: Cotton — Foreign Tariff Changes on U.S. Exports

seo.title: Chapter 52 Export Tariff Updates: Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Cotton
seo.shortDescription: What China and others changed on U.S. cotton since January 2025, what is in force today, and what is coming.
keywords: india cotton import duty us cotton

intro: China is the only foreign action that costs Chapter 52 exporters money today: on top of its normal rate on cotton it charges an extra 10% on every U.S. good, extended to January 10, 2027. China's separate 15% tariff on U.S. cotton, in force from March to November 2025, was lifted on November 10, 2025. The one thing to watch is India: its cotton import duty is waived only in short windows, so the date the current waiver lapses matters for U.S. cotton. The press reports a waiver to October 31, 2026, but no official notice for that window could be confirmed.
scope: The 9 largest markets for U.S. Chapter 52 goods (80% of 2025 exports).

upcoming.title: China's tariff exclusions for U.S. goods end
upcoming.whatHappens: China's exclusions from its 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods are valid until December 31, 2026 under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal.
upcoming.impact: For Chapter 52 the exclusions matter for cotton. If they lapse without renewal, China's older 2018–19 counter-tariffs could again apply to cotton that relied on an exclusion.

upcoming.title: China's suspension of 24 points of its extra tariff on U.S. goods ends
upcoming.whatHappens: China suspended 24 points of its extra tariff on all U.S. goods for one year from November 10, 2025, keeping 10%. Tariff Commission Announcement No. 6 of 2026 (November 9, 2026) continued the suspension for two months from November 10, 2026, to January 10, 2027.
upcoming.impact: China's extra duty would go from 10% to 34% on top of its normal rate. A $1 million shipment of raw cotton inside the quota would pay about $350,000, versus about $110,000 today.
upcoming.status: Extended to January 10, 2027; no further extension announced

inEffect.measure: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
inEffect.appliesTo: Every Chapter 52 good sold to China, on top of its normal rate: 1% for raw cotton inside China's 894,000-tonne quota and 40% above it. China's separate 15% tariff on U.S. cotton was lifted on November 10, 2025.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $1 million shipment of raw cotton inside the quota pays about $10,000 in normal duty plus $100,000 under this measure, or $110,000, versus $10,000 before 2025. From May 14 to November 10, 2025 it also paid China's separate 15% on cotton, so it paid about $260,000.

changes.title: U.S.–Thailand Agreement on Reciprocal Trade: negotiations substantially concluded
changes.status: Not yet signed; Thailand's tariffs on U.S. goods unchanged
changes.detail: Under the October 26, 2025 framework, Thailand committed to eliminate tariff barriers on about 99% of goods, covering a full range of U.S. industrial, food and agricultural products. On November 17, 2026 the two leaders announced in Manila that negotiations had reached substantial conclusion; each side must now complete its internal processes before the agreement is signed and enters into force. No Thai tariff cut has been published yet.

changes.title: India's trade-remedy authority recommends soda ash import quotas, with 159,388 tonnes a year for U.S. supply
changes.status: Recommended Nov 4, 2026; not yet notified by the Government of India
changes.detail: Final findings in India's safeguard (quantitative restrictions) case on soda ash (subheading 2836.20), opened March 16, 2026: DGTR recommends country-wise import quotas for two years, 754,992 tonnes in year 1 and 792,740 tonnes in year 2. The U.S. share is 159,388 tonnes in year 1 and 167,357 tonnes in year 2, released in four equal quarterly tranches (39,847 tonnes a quarter in year 1). Imports from the U.S. were 385,453 tonnes in January–September 2025 alone. The quotas apply only once the Central Government notifies them in the Gazette; imports under India's Advance Authorisation scheme would stay outside the quota. No tariff is involved.

changes.title: U.S.–China Board of Trade product lists
changes.status: Recommended for reduced tariffs; no Chinese tariff cut published yet
changes.detail: China's import list under the U.S.–China Board of Trade “30-for-30” framework names 1,619 Chinese tariff lines that could get lower tariffs on U.S. goods. No Chinese tariff cut has been published yet. Non-seed soybeans (Chapter 12's dominant export) were explicitly excluded from this list; the 10% extra tariff stays on them. Published summaries of China's list do not name cotton, so it is treated as not covered; no rate or start date is set.

changes.title: Counter-tariffs on U.S. products (answering U.S. Section 338 tariffs)
changes.status: In force
changes.detail: Counter-tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on listed U.S. products — steel, aluminum, dairy, furniture and clothing, but also machinery, household appliances and electronics such as smartphones, routers and monitors (50%). The order applies to goods of U.S. origin and has no exemption for goods that qualify for CUSMA.

changes.title: Saskatchewan puts a 50% levy on U.S. alcohol
changes.status: In force from September 8, 2026
changes.detail: Saskatchewan's government announced on August 27, 2026 a 50% levy on all U.S.-produced alcohol imported into the province, applied through the Saskatchewan Liquor and Gaming Authority's ordering system from September 8, 2026. It answers the 50% U.S. tariff on Canadian alcohol of August 22, 2026. It is a provincial measure: Canada's federal counter-tariffs of September 8, 2026 skip beverages.

changes.title: Mexico imposes an anti-dumping duty of US$1.72/kg on U.S. hollow aluminum profiles
changes.status: In force from 2026-09-05 (provisional US$1.62/kg from Dec 31, 2025)
changes.detail: Secretaría de Economía final resolution in case AD_28-24 (DOF, September 4, 2026): a definitive anti-dumping duty of US$1.72 per kilogram on hollow aluminum profiles (tariff fraction 7604.21.01) originating in the United States, and US$1.93 per kilogram on those from China, whatever the country they are shipped from. The preliminary resolution of December 31, 2025 had set provisional duties of US$1.62 and US$1.88 per kilogram. It is a trade-remedy case, not a general counter-tariff, and applies on top of the USMCA rate.

changes.title: Brazil has imposed nothing on U.S. goods; it is challenging U.S. tariffs at the WTO
changes.status: Nothing imposed on U.S. goods; talks ongoing
changes.detail: Brazil has published no countermeasure on U.S. goods. Its Economic Reciprocity Law (Law 15,122 of April 11, 2025) would allow them — such as import restrictions or suspending intellectual-property obligations — but none has been applied. On July 27, 2026 Brazil asked the United States for WTO consultations over U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and Brazilian ministers met USTR on August 31 and September 30, 2026 to set up a working group on a possible agreement.

changes.title: EU extends suspension of its Boeing/Airbus-dispute retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods
changes.status: Suspended since July 11, 2021; extended by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 from July 11, 2026
changes.detail: The U.S. and EU suspended, for five years from July 11, 2021, the tariffs each had imposed or threatened in their 17-year WTO dispute over Boeing and Airbus subsidies (the EU's WTO-authorized countermeasures covered up to $4 billion of U.S. goods, large civil aircraft among them, under the Cooperative Framework for Large Civil Aircraft). Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 of July 6, 2026 extends the EU's suspension past its July 10, 2026 expiry; the U.S. has not reactivated its Section 301 tariffs from the same dispute either.

changes.title: USMCA stays in force: Canada and Mexico keep 0% on qualifying U.S. goods
changes.status: USMCA still in force
changes.detail: At the first USMCA joint review on July 1, 2026 the three countries did not agree to a new 16-year term, so the agreement is now reviewed every year; it stays in force until at least July 1, 2036. Canada and Mexico keep applying USMCA rates to qualifying U.S. goods.

changes.title: EU renews 0% duty on live and frozen lobster to July 31, 2030 and adds processed lobster
changes.status: In force from June 30, 2026; applies retroactively from August 1, 2025 to July 31, 2030
changes.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1461 of June 25, 2026 sets a 0% EU duty on live lobster (CN 0306 32 10), frozen lobster (0306 12 10, 0306 12 90) and frozen rock lobster (0306 11 90) and, for the first time, on prepared or preserved lobster (1605 30 90). It renews the zero duty of the 2020 U.S.–EU lobster deal (Regulation (EU) 2020/2131), which ran from August 1, 2020 to July 31, 2025, as agreed in the August 2025 EU–U.S. Joint Statement. In the gap the normal EU rates applied (8% on live lobster, 6% or 16% on frozen lobster, 12.5% on frozen rock lobster); duties paid between August 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026 are refunded on request. Like the 2020 regulation, the 0% applies to lobster from every country. The Commission can suspend it if the U.S. stops implementing the Joint Statement, and must assess it by January 31, 2030.

changes.title: EU–U.S. framework tariff cuts adopted
changes.status: In force (applies from July 1, 2026)
changes.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 cuts EU duties on listed U.S. goods to zero from July 1, 2026, and Regulation (EU) 2026/1461 sets aside duties on certain other goods. For Chapter 52 the relevant part is the cut to zero on U.S. industrial goods, which includes cotton yarn and fabric; raw cotton is already duty-free in the EU.

changes.title: South Africa keeps its 40% anti-dumping duty on U.S. soda ash after a sunset review
changes.status: Maintained (final determination published Feb 19, 2026)
changes.detail: South Africa's International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC) opened a sunset review of the anti-dumping duty on disodium carbonate (soda ash, tariff heading 2836.20) from the U.S. on March 7, 2025, at the request of Botswana Ash. No U.S. exporter or SACU importer responded. ITAC found that ending the duty would likely lead to renewed dumping and injury, and the Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition approved keeping the 40% duty (Notice 3778 of 2026). The duty applies at the border of the Southern African Customs Union (South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Eswatini). It is a trade-remedy case, not a general counter-tariff.

changes.title: U.S.–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade: Taiwan cuts tariffs on U.S. goods
changes.status: Signed Feb. 12, 2026; Taiwan's legislature must still approve it
changes.detail: Taiwan agrees to eliminate or reduce 99% of its tariff barriers on U.S. goods, with preferential access for wheat, beef, pork, lamb, dairy, tree nuts and other farm goods, and plans to buy $44.4 billion of U.S. LNG and crude oil from 2025 through 2029. The USTR fact sheet gives no entry-into-force date or phase-in schedule: Taiwan must first submit the agreement to its legislature. For Chapter 52 the relevant part is Taiwan's broad tariff cuts on industrial goods, which would include cotton yarn and fabric; Taiwan has not published rates or a start date.

changes.title: U.S.–Bangladesh Agreement on Reciprocal Trade: Bangladesh sets purchase goals for U.S. wheat, soy, cotton and LNG
changes.status: Signed Feb. 9, 2026
changes.detail: Bangladesh endeavors to buy about $3.5 billion of U.S. farm goods, including wheat (at least 700,000 tonnes a year for five years), soy and cotton, and about $15 billion of U.S. energy over 15 years, including long-term LNG contracts, and agrees to accept U.S. sanitary and phytosanitary certificates. The U.S. keeps a 19% rate on most Bangladeshi goods. The agreement sets purchase goals and does not itself change Bangladesh's tariffs on U.S. goods. For Chapter 52 the relevant part is the cotton purchase goal, within the $3.5 billion farm total.

changes.title: U.S.–India interim trade framework: India to cut tariffs on U.S. industrial and farm goods
changes.status: Framework announced Feb. 6, 2026; interim agreement not yet confirmed signed
changes.detail: India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all U.S. industrial goods and a wide range of U.S. food and farm products, including dried distillers' grains, red sorghum for animal feed, tree nuts, fruit, soybean oil and wine and spirits. India also intends to buy $500 billion of U.S. energy, aircraft and parts, precious metals, technology products and coking coal over five years. It is a framework for an interim agreement: no rates or start dates are published. For Chapter 52 cotton is not named; the relevant part is the cut on U.S. industrial goods, which includes cotton yarn and fabric.

changes.title: Mexico raises its general tariffs on goods from countries without a trade agreement
changes.status: In force since Jan 1, 2026; U.S. goods still enter under USMCA
changes.detail: The decree raises Mexico's general (MFN) rates on more than 1,400 tariff lines, mostly cars, textiles, clothing, steel, plastics and footwear. U.S. goods that qualify for USMCA keep their preferential rate. Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods. Chapter 52 yarn and fabric are among the textile lines Mexico raised, but U.S. goods that qualify for USMCA keep 0%.

changes.title: Canada's 25% global surtax on steel derivative goods, U.S. goods included
changes.now: 25% surtax on listed steel derivative goods
changes.status: In force since December 26, 2025
changes.detail: Canada's Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order (SOR/2025-267) charges a 25% surtax on the full value of listed steel derivative goods from every country, the United States included, such as prefabricated buildings, wire, cables, chains, fasteners and wind towers. It is not a counter-tariff aimed at the U.S.: it answers global steel overcapacity and the diversion caused by U.S. steel tariffs, and the Government of Canada put 44% of the C$10.6 billion of goods it covers as imported from the United States. Goods already paying another Canadian surtax (such as the United States Surtax Orders on steel and aluminum and of 2026) do not pay it again, and goods imported before July 1, 2027 for making motor vehicles, aircraft or their parts are exempt (SOR/2026-155).

changes.title: China opens an expiry review of its 214.9–222.0% anti-dumping duties on U.S. EPDM rubber, keeping them in force
changes.status: Expiry review under way; ruling due before December 20, 2026
changes.detail: MOFCOM Announcement No. 81 of 2025: China has charged anti-dumping duties on ethylene-propylene-non-conjugated diene rubber (EPDM, Chinese lines 4002.7010 and 4002.7090) from the U.S., Korea and the EU since December 20, 2020 (Announcement No. 60 of 2020), at 214.9–222.0% for U.S. companies (Dow 222.0%, ExxonMobil 214.9%, Arlanxeo USA and Lion Copolymer Geismar 219.8%, all others 222.0%). On a request from PetroChina Jilin Petrochemical and SINOPEC Mitsui Elastomers, MOFCOM opened an expiry review from December 20, 2025, which must end before December 20, 2026; the duties stay in force while it runs. It is a trade-remedy case, not a general counter-tariff.

changes.title: Reciprocity petition against the 2025 U.S. tariffs: framing approved, action deferred
changes.status: Never applied
changes.detail: Camex's executive committee (Gecex) approved the Foreign Ministry's petition as falling under the Economic Reciprocity Law and chose to await diplomatic consultations before forming the working group that would propose countermeasures. Nothing was imposed.

changes.title: U.S.–UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement
changes.status: In force; full text agreed Apr 2, 2026
changes.detail: Not a tariff: the UK raises the net price it pays for new medicines by about 25% and lifts NICE’s cost-effectiveness threshold. UK tariffs on medicines stay at zero.

changes.title: U.S.–Switzerland–Liechtenstein trade framework
changes.status: Framework; full agreement under negotiation
changes.detail: Switzerland intends to apply zero duties on all U.S. industrial goods. Switzerland already applies no industrial tariffs to any origin, so this changes little for cotton.

changes.title: China extends its tariff exclusions for U.S. goods to December 31, 2026
changes.status: Exclusions valid until Dec 31, 2026
changes.detail: Under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal, China extended its market-based exclusion process for imports from the United States; exclusions stay valid until December 31, 2026. They lift China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering the U.S. Section 301 tariffs), which were never repealed. For Chapter 52 the exclusions matter for cotton, which China's 2018–19 counter-tariffs hit.

changes.title: India ends duty-free yellow peas: 30% duty on imports from every country, U.S. included
changes.status: In force since November 1, 2025
changes.detail: Customs Notification No. 46/2025 of October 29, 2025 charges a 10% basic customs duty and a 20% Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess on yellow peas (Indian tariff item 0713 10 10) shipped on a bill of lading dated November 1, 2025 or later, ending the duty-free treatment India had given yellow peas since December 2023. It is not aimed at the U.S.: it applies to yellow peas from every country, to support Indian pulse prices. Imports stay "Free" (no minimum import price or port restriction, but registration in India's online Import Monitoring System) for bills of lading dated up to March 31, 2027 (DGFT Notification No. 70/2025-26).

changes.title: India opens an anti-dumping investigation into U.S. halobutyl rubber
changes.status: Investigation; no duty published as far as we found
changes.detail: India's Directorate General of Trade Remedies (case AD(OI)-51/2025) opened an anti-dumping investigation on October 31, 2025 into halo-isobutene-isoprene rubber (bromobutyl and chlorobutyl, mainly 4002.39) from the United States, China and Singapore, on an application by Reliance Sibur Elastomers. An earlier DGTR recommendation of December 2024 to put anti-dumping duties on halobutyl rubber from the U.S. and four other countries was not imposed. India separately charges US$781–859 per tonne on U.S. butyl rubber (4002.31) under Notification 17/2024-Customs (ADD) of September 27, 2024.

changes.title: U.S.–Malaysia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade signed; Malaysia has not ratified it
changes.status: Signed Oct 26, 2025; not ratified, not in force
changes.detail: Malaysia agreed to apply the duties in its Schedule 1 to U.S.-origin goods: many lines go to 0% on entry into force, others are cut over up to 10 or 15 years, and some stay at today's rate. The agreement enters into force 60 days after both sides exchange written notifications. Malaysia's trade ministry said on February 21, 2026 that it has signed but not ratified the agreement, so Malaysia's normal (MFN) rates still apply to U.S. goods.

changes.title: India's trade-remedy authority recommends anti-dumping duties on U.S. soda ash; no duty imposed
changes.status: Recommended Sept 29, 2025; never imposed
changes.detail: DGTR's final findings in case AD (OI)-29/2024 recommended five-year anti-dumping duties on soda ash (2836.20) from Turkey, Russia, the U.S. and Iran: US$27 per tonne on Sisecam Wyoming and US$79 per tonne on other U.S. producers (the November 4, 2025 corrigendum changed only the Turkish rates). India's Ministry of Finance did not impose them: DGTR's November 2026 safeguard findings record that the case 'did not result in the imposition of duty'. Separately, India's DGFT barred soda ash imports priced below ₹20,108 per tonne CIF from December 30, 2024 to December 31, 2025 (a minimum import price, Notification No. 46/2024-25, extended once); it has lapsed.

changes.title: U.S.–Japan agreement
changes.status: In force
changes.detail: Executive Order 14345 implements the U.S.–Japan agreement: Japan works toward buying U.S. farm and other goods worth $8 billion a year and investing in the U.S. The agreement does not mention cotton.

changes.title: EU countermeasures on about €93B of U.S. goods
changes.status: Suspended, never applied
changes.detail: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564 listed about €93B of U.S. goods for extra duties from September 7, 2025. The measures were suspended from August 6, 2025, again from February 7, 2026, and from August 7, 2026 with no end date (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1893). Chapter 52 goods were not found among the annex product groups described in public summaries; the measures are suspended with no end date, so nothing is charged.

changes.title: Mexico resets its anti-dumping duty on U.S. liquid caustic soda to US$195 per tonne
changes.before: Reference-price duty: the shortfall below US$288.71/t (max 54.79%)
changes.now: US$195 per tonne (dry basis) anti-dumping duty
changes.status: In force from May 30, 2025; sunset review open since July 11, 2025
changes.detail: Mexico has charged an anti-dumping duty on liquid caustic soda (sodium hydroxide in aqueous solution, tariff fraction 2815.12.01) from the U.S. since 1995. A review resolution published May 29, 2025 replaced the reference-price scheme (a duty equal to the shortfall below US$288.71 per tonne, capped at 54.79%) with a specific duty of US$195 per tonne, measured dry or at 100% concentration, on U.S.-origin goods whatever the country they are shipped from. Mexico's Ministry of Economy opened a sunset review (case EC_17-25) on July 11, 2025; the duty stays in force while it runs. It applies on top of the USMCA rate.

changes.title: Mexico keeps its US$0.34075/kg anti-dumping duty on U.S. emulsion SBR rubber for five more years
changes.status: In force; extended for five years from January 26, 2024
changes.detail: Secretaría de Economía final resolution in the expiry and ex officio review E.C. Rev. 24/23 (DOF, May 29, 2025): the anti-dumping duty on emulsion styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) of tariff items 4002.19.01, 4002.19.02, 4002.19.03 and 4002.19.99 is kept unchanged at US$0.34075 per kilogram for all U.S. exporters (it also covers Korea and Japan) and extended for five years from January 26, 2024. It is a trade-remedy duty and applies on top of the USMCA rate.

changes.title: China imposes anti-dumping duties of up to 74.9% on U.S. polyoxymethylene (POM) copolymer
changes.status: In force from 2025-05-19 for five years (deposits from 2025-01-24)
changes.detail: MOFCOM Announcement No. 25 of 2025 (final ruling of 2025-05-18): anti-dumping duties on POM copolymer (HS 3907.1010 and 3907.1090) from the U.S., EU, Taiwan and Japan. The rate for all U.S. companies, including Ticona Polymers, is 74.9%. It is a trade-remedy case, not a general counter-tariff, and covers only this one resin.

changes.title: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
changes.status: In force; 24-point suspension extended to Jan 10, 2027
changes.detail: Rose 34% → 84% → 125% in April 2025 (125% from April 12), then cut to 10% from May 14, 2025 with 24 points suspended for 90 days. The suspension was extended for 90 days from August 12, 2025 and for one year from November 10, 2025, with the 10% kept. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027. Applies to every U.S.-origin good on top of China’s normal rate.

changes.title: India notifies the WTO of possible retaliation for U.S. steel and aluminum tariffs; nothing applied
changes.status: Notified to the WTO; never applied
changes.detail: India told the WTO on May 12, 2025 (G/SG/N/12/IND/5) that it reserved the right to suspend concessions on U.S. goods to offset U.S. Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminum, covering US$7.6 billion of Indian exports; it raised the duty figure to US$3.82 billion on July 9, 2025 after the U.S. moved to 50%. Similar notices followed for auto parts (July 4, 2025) and copper (October 30, 2025). None named products or rates, and India has published no customs notification applying them.

changes.title: U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal
changes.status: In force
changes.detail: UK concessions were a beef quota and a duty-free ethanol quota.

changes.title: 25% surtax on U.S. passenger vehicles and light trucks (non-U.S. content for CUSMA-compliant vehicles)
changes.now: 25% on non-U.S. content (full value if not CUSMA-compliant)
changes.status: In force; kept when Canada removed most 2025 counter-tariffs on Sept 1, 2025
changes.detail: Canada's United States Surtax Order (Motor Vehicles 2025), SOR/2025-118: a 25% surtax on U.S. passenger vehicles and light trucks (8703, 8704). A CUSMA-compliant vehicle pays it only on its non-U.S. content; a non-compliant vehicle pays on its full value. Auto parts are not covered.

changes.title: China's extra tariffs of 10% and 15% on U.S. farm goods, lifted November 10, 2025
changes.status: Lifted on November 10, 2025
changes.detail: Tariff Commission Announcement No. 2 of 2025 (March 4) added 15% on U.S. chicken, wheat, corn and cotton and 10% on sorghum, soybeans, pork, beef, aquatic products, fruits, vegetables and dairy from March 10, 2025, answering the U.S. fentanyl tariffs. Announcement No. 9 of 2025 (November 5) stopped them from November 10, 2025, under the U.S.–China deal. China's separate extra tariff on all U.S. goods stays.

changes.title: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods
changes.status: Mostly removed Sept 1, 2025
changes.detail: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods. Canada repealed most of it on Sept 1, 2025, keeping only the steel, aluminum and auto surtaxes.

changes.title: China's customs suspends all imports of U.S. logs, lifted November 10, 2025
changes.status: Lifted November 10, 2025
changes.detail: China's customs administration (GACC) suspended imports of U.S. logs from March 4, 2025 (GACC Announcement No. 29 of 2025), saying it had found quarantine pests such as bark beetles and longhorn beetles in U.S. shipments. It came the same day as China's first counter-tariffs on U.S. farm goods. GACC Announcement No. 216 of 2025, issued November 7, 2025 after the U.S.–China deal, repealed the suspension from November 10, 2025. No tariff was involved; logs pay China's normal rate plus its extra tariff on all U.S. goods.

changes.title: Canadian provinces pull U.S. alcohol from government liquor stores
changes.status: Most provinces still not buying U.S. alcohol in late 2026
changes.detail: Not a tariff: from March 2025 most provincial liquor boards, which control alcohol sales in Canada, stopped buying and selling U.S. beer, wine and spirits. As of their latest official statements, British Columbia is retaining its ban (September 2026), Quebec's March 4, 2025 order to remove U.S. products stands, and Nova Scotia is not importing U.S. alcohol (September 2026). Alberta resumed sales in June 2025, and Saskatchewan now charges a 50% levy on U.S. alcohol (see that entry).

changes.title: India cuts its tariff on bourbon whiskey from 150% to 100%
changes.status: In force since February 13, 2025
changes.detail: Customs Notification No. 14/2025 (February 13, 2025) lowered India's agriculture infrastructure and development cess (AIDC) on bourbon whiskey (2208 30 11 and 2208 30 91) from 100% to 50%, so bourbon pays 100% in all instead of 150%. The cut applies to bourbon from any country, but the U.S. is its only source; other whiskies, spirits and wine still pay 150%.

changes.title: China's extra tariffs on U.S. coal and LNG (15%) and on crude oil, farm machinery, large cars and pickups (10%)
changes.status: In force
changes.detail: Tariff Commission Announcement No. 1 of 2025 (February 4) added 15% on U.S. coal and liquefied natural gas and 10% on crude oil, agricultural machinery, large-engine cars and pickup trucks from February 10, 2025, answering the U.S. fentanyl tariffs. Announcement No. 9 of 2025 ended only the March 2025 farm-goods tariffs, so these remain.
